text.title: Shard, Build, Or Leave It
text.summary: Routing from the measured index share and the corpus shape to one action. Free actions are exhausted before any paid one is considered.

decision-tree.root-question: From the upstream cost ledger: what share of a lookup is index reads, does the corpus nest under a natural key, and does any single index exceed the declared ceiling?

conclusion.verdict: LEAVE ALONE. The bill is candidates or bodies, not the map. Declare the ceiling anyway so future growth trips a check, and go optimise the tier that is actually paying.

COMPRESS ENTRIES FIRST. Replace restated summaries with a discriminator under the declared cap and re-measure before anything else. It is free, reversible, needs no re-routing, and usually removes the ceiling breach on its own.

branch.when: index_share >= 0.2 AND entries_already_compressed == true AND corpus_nests_naturally == true

conclusion.verdict: SHARD. Split every index above the trigger on its natural partition key, leave a stub at the original path carrying one row per shard, and audit reachability. No model is invoked; build_tokens stays zero.

branch.when: index_share >= 0.2 AND entries_already_compressed == true AND corpus_nests_naturally == false AND corpus_changes_often == false

conclusion.verdict: BUILD A RECURSIVE SUMMARY TREE. Authorised only here — no natural key, and a static corpus that amortises the build. Record build_tokens and the rebuild trigger; expect roughly a sixth of a full extraction-graph build on the same corpus.

branch.when: index_share >= 0.2 AND corpus_nests_naturally == false AND corpus_changes_often == true

conclusion.verdict: STOP AND FIND A KEY. A summary tree over a frequently changing corpus repays its build on every change. Impose a partition key — by source, by owner, by date — and shard on that instead; an imperfect free hierarchy beats a perfect one that is never rebuilt.
OVERLAY: widen, do not deepen. Every level is a full read on every lookup. Increase fan-out to hold the corpus at the current depth before adding a tier, and never exceed depth 3.

OVERLAY, whichever branch applied: delegate the walk to a retrieval subagent that returns leaf paths and one-line reasons. An index read into a long-lived context is re-sent every turn, so its cost is the read multiplied by the remaining session.
